agent_value.quote: AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification. Copyright (c) 2003-2020 Arm Limited or its affiliates. ARM IHI 0022H (ID040120)
31 March 2020 | H | Non-Confidential | EAC-0 release of version H. New optional features defined for AMBA 5 interface variants.

The AMBA 3 AXI protocol release is referred to as AXI3. The AMBA 4 AXI protocol releases are referred to as AXI4 and AXI4-Lite. The AMBA 5 AXI protocol releases are referred to as AXI5 and AXI5-Lite. The AMBA 4 ACE protocol releases are referred to as ACE and ACE-Lite. The AMBA 5 ACE protocol releases are referred to as: ACE5, ACE5-Lite, ACE5-LiteDVM, ACE5-LiteACP.

The AMBA AXI protocol supports high-performance, high-frequency system designs ... It is suitable for high-bandwidth and low-latency designs ... Separate address/control and data phases ... Support for unaligned data transfers, using byte strobes ... Uses burst-based transactions with only the start address issued ... Separate read and write data channels, that can provide low-cost Direct Memory Access (DMA) ... Support for issuing multiple outstanding addresses ... Support for out-of-order transaction completion ... Permits easy addition of register stages to provide timing closure ... It is backward-compatible with AHB and APB interfaces.
The AXI protocol is burst-based and defines five independent transaction channels: Read address (AR), Read data (R), Write address (AW), Write data (W), Write response (B).

agent_value.quote: The data bus, which can be 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, or 1024 bits wide.
Most systems use one of three interconnect topologies: Shared address and data buses; Shared address buses and multiple data buses; Multilayer, with multiple address and data buses.
A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary.
AXI3 supports burst lengths of 1-16 transfers, for all burst types. AXI4 extends burst length support for the INCR burst type to 1-256 transfers.

agent_value.text: All five transaction channels use the same VALID/READY handshake. Source generates VALID; destination generates READY. Transfer occurs only when both VALID and READY are HIGH at a rising edge of ACLK.
A source must not wait until READY is asserted before asserting VALID. Once VALID is asserted, it must remain asserted until the handshake occurs.
A destination is permitted to wait for VALID to be asserted before asserting READY. If READY is asserted, it is permitted to deassert READY before VALID is asserted.
On master and slave interfaces, there must be no combinatorial paths between input and output signals.
Each AXI interface has a single clock signal ACLK. All input signals are sampled on the rising edge of ACLK; all output signal changes can only occur after the rising edge of ACLK.
Reset signal ARESETn is active-LOW. Reset can be asserted asynchronously, but deassertion must be synchronous to ACLK.
During reset, master must drive ARVALID, AWVALID, WVALID LOW. Slave must drive RVALID and BVALID LOW. Earliest point a master may begin driving xVALID HIGH is the ACLK edge after ARESETn is HIGH.
Channel handshake dependency rule (anti-deadlock): The VALID of a sending interface must not be dependent on the READY of the receiving interface.
agent_value.source: A3.3.1 Dependencies between channel handshake signals

agent_value.text: Read dependency: slave must wait for both ARVALID and ARREADY to be asserted before asserting RVALID.
AXI3 write dependency: slave must wait for WVALID, WREADY, and WLAST before asserting BVALID.
AXI4/AXI5 additional write dependency: slave must wait for AWVALID, AWREADY, WVALID, and WREADY all asserted before asserting BVALID. The slave must also wait for WLAST before BVALID.
A write response must always follow the last write transfer in a write transaction.
Read data must always follow the read address of the data.
A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary.
For wrapping bursts, the burst length must be 2, 4, 8, or 16; start address must be aligned to the size of each transfer.
Early termination of bursts is not supported. To reduce data transferred in a write burst, the master may deassert all write strobes but must complete all transfers.
The master must assert WLAST while it is driving the final write transfer in the burst.
The slave must assert RLAST when it is driving the final read transfer in the burst.
When WVALID is LOW, the write strobes can take any value; spec recommends they are either driven LOW or held at their previous value.
Protocol requires that the required number of data transfers must be performed even if an error is reported. The remainder of the burst is not cancelled if the slave gives a single error response.
agent_value.source: A3.4.5 Read and write response structure

agent_value.text: For a write transaction, a single response is signaled for the entire burst, not for each data transfer.
In a read transaction, the slave can signal different responses for different transfers in a burst.
There is one write strobe for each 8 bits of the write data bus; WSTRB[n] corresponds to WDATA[(8n)+7:(8n)].
A master must issue write data in the same order that it issues the transaction addresses.
The interleaving of write data with different IDs was permitted in AXI3 but is deprecated in AXI4 and later.
When a master issues a write request, it must be able to provide all write data for that transaction without dependency on other transactions from that master.
When a master issues a read request, it must be able to accept all read data for that transaction without dependency on other transactions from that master.
All transactions with a given AXI ID value must remain in order; no restriction on ordering of transactions with different ID values.
The slave must ensure that the RID value of any returned data matches the ARID value of the address it is responding to.

The ordering model does not give any ordering guarantees between: transactions from different masters; read and write transactions; transactions with different IDs; transactions to different Peripheral regions; transactions to different Memory locations.
In AXI4, all Device transactions using the same ID to the same slave must be ordered with respect to each other.
Slave must also wait for WLAST to be asserted before asserting BVALID, because BRESP must be signaled only after the last data transfer of a write transaction.

agent_value: Master issues an exclusive read with some ARID at address X.
Slave that supports exclusive monitors X for that ARID.
Master later issues exclusive write with AWID matching ARID at the same address X.
If no other master wrote to X since the exclusive read -> slave returns EXOKAY, write updates memory.
If another master wrote to X -> slave returns OKAY (failure), write is NOT applied.
Slave that does not support exclusive returns OKAY for both normal and exclusive accesses (master treats as error).

A master performs an exclusive read ... at some later time the master attempts the exclusive write to the same address, with an AWID that matches the ARID used for the exclusive read. The exclusive write is signaled as either Successful (EXOKAY) if no other master has written ... or Failed (OKAY) if another master has written.

The number of bytes to be transferred in an exclusive access burst must be a power of 2, that is, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, or 128 bytes. The maximum number of bytes that can be transferred in an exclusive burst is 128. The burst length for an exclusive access must not exceed 16 transfers.
AWQOS / ARQOS: a 4-bit QoS identifier. A default value of 0b0000 indicates that the interface is not participating in any QoS scheme. A higher value indicates a higher priority transaction.

agent_value.name: Reset behavior

agent_value.name: VALID/READY handshake compliance
scenarios: Source asserts VALID and holds info stable until READY (no premature retract).
Destination asserts READY ahead of VALID; transfer occurs in one cycle when VALID arrives.
Both assert same cycle.
Source does NOT wait for READY before VALID.

agent_value.name: FIXED burst with WSTRB variation per beat (FIFO emulation).
scenarios: AxBURST=0b00 with same AxADDR each beat; WSTRB varies.

agent_value.name: INCR burst aligned/unaligned/length 1..256
scenarios: 32-bit transfers on 32-bit bus, address 0x00, length 4 (aligned).
32-bit transfers on 32-bit bus, address 0x01 (unaligned), length 4.
32-bit transfers on 64-bit bus, address 0x07, length 5 (unaligned, partial first beat).
AXI4 INCR length up to 256.

agent_value.name: WRAP burst at cache-line boundaries
scenarios: WRAP length must be one of 2,4,8,16.
Start address must be aligned to AxSIZE.
Address wraps to Wrap_Boundary when reaching upper bound.

agent_value.name: 4KB boundary enforcement
scenarios: Burst that would cross a 4KB boundary must be rejected/split by master; no slave may receive such a burst.

agent_value.name: WLAST/RLAST correctness
scenarios: WLAST must assert exactly once, on the final write beat.
RLAST must assert exactly once, on the final read beat.

agent_value.name: In-order completion for same-ID transactions
scenarios: Issue two reads with same ARID; RID must echo and responses must arrive in issue order.

agent_value.name: Out-of-order completion for different IDs
scenarios: Issue two reads with different ARID; slave may complete in any order.

agent_value.name: Exclusive access read-modify-write
scenarios: Exclusive read followed by exclusive write from same master with matching ID at same address -> EXOKAY.
Exclusive read; another master writes; exclusive write -> OKAY (fail) with no memory update.
Exclusive access to slave that does not support -> OKAY for both phases.

agent_value.name: Error response handling
scenarios: SLVERR for unsupported transfer / read-only-location write / timeout.
DECERR from default slave for undecoded address.
Error must still complete required number of beats (no early termination).

agent_value.name: Inactive byte lanes
scenarios: WSTRB LOW for byte lanes that don't carry valid data; recommended WDATA=0 for inactive lanes.

agent_value.name: Deadlock avoidance
scenarios: Master must not wait for AWREADY before driving WVALID (would deadlock if slave waits for WVALID first).
Slave VALID must not be combinationally dependent on its incoming READY.

agent_value.name: AXI4 BVALID waits for AW + W + WLAST
scenarios: AXI4/AXI5 slave must not assert BVALID until both AW and W handshakes complete and WLAST is seen.

agent_value.name: AXI4 write data interleaving forbidden
scenarios: AXI4+ master must issue write data in the address-channel order; no WID interleaving.

agent_value.name: Default values when optional signals omitted
scenarios: AWBURST absent -> assume INCR.
AWSIZE absent -> assume data bus width.
WSTRB absent -> assume all ones.

agent_value: 1. Master drives ARID, ARADDR, ARLEN, ARSIZE, ARBURST, ARLOCK, ARCACHE, ARPROT, ARQOS, ARREGION; asserts ARVALID.
2. Slave eventually asserts ARREADY; AR handshake completes at rising ACLK.
3. Slave drives first beat on RDATA with RID=ARID, RRESP, RLAST=0 (or 1 if length=1); asserts RVALID.
4. Master asserts RREADY; beat handshake completes.
5. Repeat for each beat with incrementing/wrapping/fixed address per AxBURST.
6. Slave asserts RLAST=1 on the final beat.
7. Master accepts final beat; transaction complete.

agent_value: 1. Master drives AWID, AWADDR, AWLEN, AWSIZE, AWBURST, AWLOCK, AWCACHE, AWPROT, AWQOS, AWREGION; asserts AWVALID.
2. Master may concurrently drive WDATA[0], WSTRB, WLAST=0 (or 1 if single beat); asserts WVALID.
3. AW and W handshakes complete (in any order; W data can lead, lag, or be concurrent with AW).
4. Master drives subsequent W beats with WLAST=1 on the final beat.
5. After AWVALID+AWREADY+WVALID+WREADY+WLAST all observed by slave, slave asserts BVALID with BID=AWID and BRESP.
6. Master asserts BREADY; B handshake completes; transaction done.

agent_value: 1. Master issues exclusive read: ARLOCK = Exclusive at address X with ARID=I.
2. Slave records (X, I) in its exclusive monitor; returns EXOKAY.
3. Master later issues exclusive write at X with AWID=I and AWLOCK=Exclusive.
4. Slave checks monitor: if (X,I) still valid (no intervening write to X) -> updates memory, returns EXOKAY.
5. If another master wrote X in between -> slave returns OKAY, write is NOT applied.
6. Master that gets OKAY (instead of EXOKAY) must retry the entire RMW or treat as failure.

agent_value: 1. Master ensures no other outstanding transactions before starting.
2. Master issues transactions with AxLOCK=Locked (0b10) and same AxID.
3. Interconnect arbiter blocks all other masters until master issues a final unlocking transaction (AxLOCK != Locked).
4. Master must complete locked sequence before any further transactions.
Note: AXI4 removes locked-access support; AXI4 only supports Normal and Exclusive.
